assessments.title: Bottleneck code-review workbench
assessments.source_version_note: Repository master public description inspected 2026-10-23; no release version pinned
source_observations: README describes Electron + React/TypeScript, Monaco diff review, local SQLite cache, incremental GitHub GraphQL sync, prefix-grouped PRs, and bulk PR actions.
GitHub repository metadata lists MIT license and last pushed 2025-12-04. This is a source snapshot, not a live quality verification.
assessments.ghostmesh_problem: Too many simultaneous agent-generated PRs and review receipts create operator attention bottlenecks.
assessments.unexpected_connection: An account first surfaced as a contributor to agentops-ai/agentops also owns a public desktop code-review workbench, which is closer to GhostMesh operator attention management than its initial contributor attribution implied.
assessments.strongest_objection: A faster UI for GitHub PRs is not the same as GhostMesh's evidence custody, owner authority, task identity, cross-surface continuation, or approval policy. Bulk merge operations increase impact if mistakenly bound to automation.
missing_evidence: No hands-on review of application behavior
No measured comparison to current owner review flow
No verified personal identity or contact interest
assessments.small_test: Read-only offline audit of 12 historical agent PR records, comparing present review steps against mock Bottleneck-style batching. Score time-to-locate-a-change, missed review context, and incorrect action affordances. No installation, OAuth grants, bulk action, or merge.

assessments.title: InspectorRAGet RAG evaluation introspection
assessments.source_version_note: arXiv v2, 2025-05-01; IBM repository main metadata inspected 2026-10-23
source_observations: Paper describes aggregate and instance-level RAG evaluation with human/algorithmic scores, metric correlation, inter-annotator agreement and model comparisons.
Standardized JSON includes dataset instances, retrieved contexts, response outputs, metric metadata, evaluator scores and annotator data.
Authors describe a stateless NextJS-based introspection UI; empirical examples support research-use observations, not guaranteed GhostMesh quality improvements.
Public IBM code repository lists Apache-2.0 license and was pushed 2026-10-20.
assessments.ghostmesh_problem: Scout claim reviews and Readers research need to surface disagreement, source quality and individual exceptions without drowning editors in aggregate scores.
assessments.unexpected_connection: A possible same-name byline trail from an arXiv paper about query clarification led to a mature RAG evaluation introspection system with explicit human-annotator disagreement and individual-case review.
assessments.strongest_objection: Its benchmark experiment format targets RAG model outputs, not Scout editorial claim provenance or human-authority workflows; adapting its interface without measuring the real gap could add redundant dashboard machinery.
missing_evidence: No reproduced evaluation on GhostMesh receipts
No independent contributor identity mapping from repeated author name
No established need beyond existing Scout history and claim-impact views
assessments.small_test: Use 12 owner-private redacted claim histories. Measure current time-to-explain a disputed recommendation and missed provenance, then compare a minimal instance-level disagreement table inspired by the paper. Require better performance than current UI before any implementation.

selection_limit: Two source-derived cases selected from the first 21 public work trails, not a ranked representative sample
